The proof uses induction with inequalities (2.1) and (2.2). This is a standard result (well-known greedy argument). Let me check the proof carefully.

Lemma 2 part 1: Strategy: always claim a currently longest unclaimed piece. Induction: if it's your turn with unclaimed multiset B, this strategy nets at least O(B). Take b_1 (a largest). Opponent takes b_j (j≥2). By induction, you gain at least O(B \ {b_1, b_j}) ≥ O(B) - b_1 by (2.1). Total ≥ b_1 + O(B) - b_1 = O(B).

Wait, there's a subtlety: after opponent takes b_j, it's your turn again with B \ {b_1, b_j}; the greedy strategy applies by induction. That seems fine. Actually the induction hypothesis is "if it is your turn and the unclaimed multiset is B, the greedy strategy nets at least O(B) from B". After you take b_1 and opponent takes b_j, it's your turn on B' = B \ {b_1,b_j}; you continue with greedy. So you get b_1 + (greedy guarantee on B') ≥ b_1 + O(B') ≥ b_1 + O(B) - b_1 = O(B). Yes.

Actually the enumeration is fixed at the start; but after removal the multiset is the same regardless of which physical object. Fine.

Part 2: after opponent takes a_j, second player plays greedy on A \ {a_j}, getting at least O(A\{a_j}) ≥ E(A) by (2.2). Yes.

Check (2.1): O(A \ {a_1, a_j}) — removing a_1 and a_j from sorted a_1 ≥ ... ≥ a_M leaves a_2,...,a_{j-1},a_{j+1},...,a_M with a_i at rank i-1 for i<j and i-2 for i>j. So odd ranks in the remaining: i-1 odd means i even (for 2≤i≤j-1), and i-2 odd means i odd (for i>j). So O(A\{a_1,a_j}) = sum_{2≤i≤j-1, i even} a_i + sum_{i>j, i odd} a_i. That matches.

O(A) - a_1 = sum_{i≥3, i odd} a_i. Hmm, the write-up says O(A)-a_1 = sum_{3≤i≤j, i odd} a_i + sum_{i>j, i odd} a_i. Wait, sum over all odd i ≥ 3, split into i ≤ j and i > j: since i odd and i ≤ j, that's 3≤i≤j. Yes.

Then the difference: O(A\{a_1,a_j}) - (O(A)-a_1) = sum_{2≤i≤j-1, i even} a_i - sum_{3≤i≤j, i odd} a_i.

For j even: even i in [2, j-1] are 2,4,...,j-2; odd i in [3,j] are 3,5,...,j-1. So difference = (a_2 - a_3) + (a_4 - a_5) + ... + (a_{j-2} - a_{j-1}) ≥ 0. Matches.

For j odd: even i in [2,j-1]: 2,...,j-1 (j-1 even); odd i in [3,j]: 3,...,j. Difference = (a_2-a_3)+...+(a_{j-1}-a_j) ≥ 0. Matches.

(2.2): removing a_j: a_i at rank i for i<j, i-1 for i>j. O(A\{a_j}) = sum_{i<j, i odd} a_i + sum_{i>j, i even} a_i. E(A) = sum_{i even} a_i. Difference = sum_{i<j, odd} a_i - sum_{i≤j, even} a_i.
